summary: Memory works best as a governed evidence system: small addressable records, explicit provenance and successors, deterministic lookup, and observable maintenance.

points.text: Stable filenames and compact records improve recall precision because an agent can retrieve one decision or event without injecting an entire chronological log into context.
Append-mostly history is valuable only when corrections are first-class. A newer record should identify what it supersedes, why it changed, and which scopes still depend on the older statement.
An index is operational metadata, not clerical garnish. Owners, validity intervals, sensitivity, status, and successor links enable cheap filtering before semantic retrieval.
Git improves provenance and review but does not solve recall: lexical search, structured metadata, optional embeddings, and benchmarked not-found behavior are still required.
